rows.comment: Says the right thing but with a clumsy relative clause. State the limit directly.
lineComments: Relative clause is awkward; say plainly that one gap cannot show variation.
rows.replacement: from your one measured gap, so it cannot show how much your cycle varies

rows.comment: Fragment that precedes other text; states a number.
Fragment stating the current position relative to the range.
States a checkable fact with a count.
Em dash, and the closing clause is a flourish. State which days are used.
lineComments: Replace the em dash and the "only days in any of this" flourish with a plain sentence.
rows.replacement: Four numbers, one per week of the cycle, counted back from your own logged starts. You logged something on {daysByWeek} days of each week across {cycles} cycles. Only those days are used.

rows.comment: Metric name with the algorithm named.
Second sentence is vague ("has two behind it"). Say the requirement.
lineComments: Reword so the two-cycle requirement is stated directly.
rows.replacement: Each point is the middle value for one cycle day across two or more of your cycles. No cycle day has two cycles yet.

rows.comment: Em dash, aphorism ("one night is not a middle"), and "not what will" antithesis. State the rule and the limit plainly.
lineComments: Remove the em dash and the antithesis; keep the one-cycle rule and the no-prediction note.
rows.replacement: Your past cycles, summarized by cycle day. Days that only one cycle reached are left empty, because one night has no middle. This describes past cycles and does not predict the next one.

rows.comment: "between ... and" is wordy for a range.
rows.replacement: Middle of {lo} to {hi} cycles at each day.

rows.comment: "got that far" is vague and "puts next to" is loose.
lineComments: Say what is compared and what is required.
rows.replacement: This compares today with the same cycle day in your previous cycles. It needs three previous cycles that reached that day.

rows.comment: Same wording problem as the generic body.
lineComments: Say what is compared and what is required.
rows.replacement: This compares today with the same cycle day in your previous cycles. It needs three previous cycles that reached day {day}.

rows.comment: Stacked "not X" antithesis. The useful content is that readiness is unchanged and there is no training advice.
lineComments: State what the comparison does and does not alter, without the slogan.
rows.replacement: This comparison does not change your readiness score and gives no training advice.

rows.comment: Format string with concrete windows (3 weeks, n days).

"A published range" has no citation in the repo; kPublishedCycleDays in lib/ui2/screens/cycle_screen.dart is 24 to 38 days with no source named. State the number the code uses. A citation still needs adding by the owner. Also drops the "says nothing else" flourish.
lineComments: Give the 24 to 38 day range the code draws; the repo names no source for it.
rows.replacement: Off until you turn it on. It draws the days between your logged starts next to a published adult cycle range of 24 to 38 days. It shows nothing else about them.

rows.comment: "needs a long run" is vague; put the requirement first.
lineComments: State the requirement and the progress.
rows.replacement: This needs {total} gaps, about a year of logging every start. You have {n} so far.

rows.comment: "look the same from here" is loose, and "One of them" has a vague antecedent.
lineComments: Name the logged start and say why the chart is not drawn.
rows.replacement: One logged start is more than {days} days after the one before it. A missed log and a long cycle look identical in the data, so the chart is not drawn.

rows.comment: Em dash, a list ending in "and others", and a "not an answer" antithesis. Keep the clinician advice.
lineComments: List the causes in a sentence and give the action directly.
rows.replacement: Thyroid conditions, stress, weight change, contraception and PCOS can all change cycle length. This chart shows your logged data next to a published range. If your cycles fall outside it, ask a clinician.

rows.comment: Short disclaimer label; part of a safety/scope statement, keep.
Colon connector, and the closing "A shape, not a shift" is a slogan. Split into plain sentences. Leading space is kept because the text is appended.
lineComments: Split the sentence and drop the slogan.
rows.replacement: Every day drawn here is within your own night-to-night spread. The biggest gap between two days is {s}. The smallest change this can tell from noise is {n}.

rows.comment: "are not separated" is passive and unclear. Leading space kept because the text is appended.
lineComments: Say the days cannot be told apart.
rows.replacement: Your nights vary by {n} on their own, so days closer together than that cannot be told apart. The biggest gap here is {s}.

rows.comment: Em dash and a tautological clause. Keep the useful reassurance that nothing was deleted.
lineComments: Drop the em dash and the restatement.
rows.replacement: The stored rows failed to load. Nothing was deleted.

rows.replacement: Your overnight resting heart rate has been above your own baseline. This check uses that one signal and cannot identify a cause.

lineComments: Split into sentences and name the baseline.
rows.replacement: Your overnight resting heart rate has been above your own baseline. That night was {z} standard deviations {direction} your baseline. This check uses that one signal and cannot identify a cause.

rows.comment: "Worth noting" is a filler opener and does not say what to do.
rows.replacement: If it continues past a couple of days, make a note of it.
